Find the established Baylor Athletics Applied Performance house visual style used in documents/decks Eric Rash has generated before. I need the exact design tokens so I can reproduce it in a new HTML one-pager.

Search these places:
1. `/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/five-slides-generator/` — this skill owns the "5 Slides in 5 Minutes" house format and builds .pptx via pptxgenjs. Look for brand colors, fonts, layout constants, any theme/config/template files, and the pptxgenjs build script.
2. `/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/status-report/` — builds a one-page PDF for Chris Ruf. Look for any HTML/CSS template.
3. `/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/html-to-pdf/` — note how it renders (the command to invoke) so I can use it.
4. Search `~/DEV` for existing Baylor-styled HTML or CSS: `grep -ril "154734\|FFB81C\|baylor" ~/DEV --include=*.html --include=*.css --include=*.js --include=*.md -l | head -40`  (Baylor green is #154734, Baylor gold #FFB81C — check what hexes are ACTUALLY used, don't assume.)
5. Check `~/DEV/AgentAssist` and `~/DEV/CPSS_BaylorSportScience_Curriculum` for report templates or brand files.

Report back CONCRETELY:
- Exact hex colors used, and what each is used for (header bg, accent, text, rules)
- Font families (and fallbacks) actually specified
- Any logo/image asset file paths that exist on disk
- Layout conventions: header/footer structure, margins, title treatment, how section headers are styled
- The exact command/how to invoke html-to-pdf
- Paste the most relevant CSS or theme-config snippets verbatim (keep it under ~150 lines total)

If you find MULTIPLE different styles, tell me which is most recent/most used and which file is the best single reference to copy from. If you find NO established style, say so plainly rather than inventing one.

## Page setup lives in the HTML, not in flags

Headless Chrome takes page size/orientation from CSS `@page`. If the source lacks one, inject a style block before rendering (edit the file or a temp copy):

<style>

# House style

The department's own formats. Slide arc, timings, and standards below are transcribed
from `5_Sides_Content_Templates.docx` in
`~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-BaylorUniversity/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/07_EDUCATION/5slides5minutes/`
— that document is the primary source. Where this file and that document disagree, the
document wins and this file is wrong.

Four formats. **Two are wired to commands today** (deck, one-pager). Two are
transcribed and ready but not yet wired (social post, video script).

---

## The production order

From the source document, and worth keeping:

| Step | Action | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Build the 5-slide deck | Forces the core idea, the structure, and the takeaway. This is the foundation. |
| 2 | Write the social post | Distils the deck to its sharpest form. If it will not fit in 200 words, the deck needs work. |
| 3 | Script the video | The social post becomes the outline; adapt for spoken delivery. |

The one-pager slots in after step 1 for the same reason — it is the deck with the
talking points folded in, for a room you will not be standing in.

---

## Format 1 — the 5-slide deck  *(wired: `/deck`)*

### Standards

| Element | Standard |
|---|---|
| Duration | 5 minutes. Hard ceiling 7 minutes with Q&A. |
| Slides | **Exactly 5. No exceptions.** The constraint drives the clarity. |
| Audience | Cross-functional H&W staff — S&C, Athletic Medicine, Sport Science, Nutrition, Mental Health |
| Tone | Practitioner sharing with peers. Confident, accessible, not academic. |
| Depth | Surface-level *by design*. The goal is awareness plus one takeaway, not mastery. |
| Outcome | Spark curiosity. Ideally leads to a longer conversation or a full Performance School session. |

### The arc

| Slide | Time | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~45 sec | **THE HOOK** — title plus an opening question or scenario. Why should a room of diverse practitioners care? Make it cross-functional. |
| 2 | ~60 sec | **THE PROBLEM / CONTEXT** — the gap, misconception, or missed opportunity. A stat, a common scenario, or "what we typically see." Ground it in their daily reality. |
| 3 | ~75 sec | **THE INSIGHT** — the core concept. One big idea, clearly explained. A visual, analogy, or data point that sticks. No jargon that fails to cross disciplines. |
| 4 | ~60 sec | **THE APPLICATION** — so what? How it shows up across specialties. One or two examples, or "what this looks like on Monday." |
| 5 | ~45 sec | **THE TAKEAWAY** — one actionable thing. End with a question that invites the longer conversation. |

Backgrounds alternate **dark, light, dark, light, dark**. This is the visual signature
of the series; the `five-slides-generator` skill enforces it. Never break it.

### What to hand off

The `five-slides-generator` skill builds the `.pptx`. Give it, per slide: slide content
(the words on the slide) and talking points (what is said out loud). Plus:

```
TOPIC
CATEGORY            from topics/library.md
PRESENTER
CORE QUESTION       the one question this talk answers
THE ONE THING       the sentence they still know in a month
THE MISCONCEPTION   what they currently believe that is wrong
FOLLOW-UP POTENTIAL could this become a full Performance School session?
```

Its house rule, worth restating: *if you cannot explain the core idea in one sentence,
you are not ready to present it.* Scratch the surface on purpose — depth comes in the
follow-up conversation.

---

## Format 2 — the one-pager  *(wired: `/onepager`)*

**New format.** There is no template for it in the source document, so this is derived
from the deck arc and from the ShiftWave protocol card in
`~/DEV/TechEd_Prop/ShitfWave/` — the department's existing printed-artifact precedent.

### Standards

| Element | Standard |
|---|---|
| Size | One page, US Letter portrait. One page is the whole constraint. |
| Purpose | The deck for a room you are not standing in. Left on a desk, pinned in a training room, handed to a coach. |
| Audience | Same cross-functional staff, reading alone with no presenter |
| Tone | Same practitioner voice. Slightly more complete, because nobody is there to answer a question. |
| Brand | `~/DEV/TechEd_Prop/ShitfWave/baylor-brand.css` |
| Build | HTML, then the `html-to-pdf` skill. Never hand-laid-out. |

### The blocks

| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| Title + core question | The topic, and the one question this answers |
| The problem | Two to three sentences. The gap or misconception, grounded in their day. |
| The insight | The core concept, plus **one** visual. This is the block a reader remembers. |
| On Monday | Two or three concrete lines, split by specialty where that helps |
| The one thing | A single boxed sentence — the takeaway, quotable |
| Sources | Three to five, so the reader can check the work |
| Who to ask | Name and role, so a question has somewhere to go |

**Differences from the deck, deliberate:** sources are printed (a deck cites verbally),
and there is no discussion prompt (nobody is in the room), replaced by a contact line.

---

## Format 3 — the social post  *(transcribed, not yet wired)*

| Element | Standard |
|---|---|
| Platform | LinkedIn (long-form) or X (short-form) |
| Length | LinkedIn 150–250 words · X 280 characters, or a 3–5 post thread |
| Tone | Conversational, credible, practitioner-to-practitioner. Not academic, not salesy. |
| Structure | Hook → Insight → Takeaway → Engagement prompt |
| Visuals | Optional — one graphic, infographic, or quote card |
| Hashtags | 2–4 relevant tags |

| Section | Length | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Hook | 1–2 sentences | Stop the scroll. Question, surprising stat, or contrarian take. |
| Insight | 3–5 sentences | One concept explained clearly, with evidence or experience. |
| Takeaway | 1–2 sentences | One practical thing to do or think about differently. |
| Engage | 1 sentence | A question that invites practitioners to share their experience. |

Audience is **external** — peers and industry, not internal staff. Goal is thought
leadership and visibility.

---

## Format 4 — the video script  *(transcribed, not yet wired)*

| Element | Standard |
|---|---|
| Duration | 60–90 seconds. Hard ceiling 2 minutes. |
| Tone | Direct, conversational, confident. Talk to camera like a colleague, not a lecturer. |
| Format | Direct-to-camera, optional text overlays or simple graphics |
| Captions | Always. Most social video is watched with the sound off. |
| CTA | Every video ends with one clear takeaway or follow prompt. |

| Section | Time | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Hook | 5–10 sec | Bold statement or question. Land it in the first 3 seconds. |
| The Problem | 10–15 sec | The common mistake or misconception. Make the viewer feel seen. |
| The Insight | 20–30 sec | One concept, clearly explained. A stat or analogy if it helps. |
| The Fix | 15–20 sec | One practical action. "Try this tomorrow." |
| Close | 5–10 sec | Reinforce the point, then the prompt. |

House rule from the source: *write the way you talk. Read it out loud before filming.
If it sounds like a script, rewrite it until it sounds like you explaining something to
a colleague over coffee.*

---

## One topic, four formats

| | Social | Video | Deck | One-pager |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Audience** | External peers | External + internal | Internal H&W staff | Internal, reading alone |
| **Length** | 150–250 words | 60–90 sec | 5 min, 5 slides | 1 page |
| **Depth** | One insight + one takeaway | Problem → insight → fix | Hook → problem → insight → application → takeaway | Deck, plus sources |
| **Goal** | Thought leadership | Awareness, shareability | Spark curiosity | Reference after the room empties |

The core idea never changes across formats. Depth, length, and audience do. All four are
written from the **same brief** — see `briefs/README.md`.

---

## Where the rendering lives

Do not reproduce any of this in code here.

- **Deck** — the `five-slides-generator` skill at
  `~/.claude/skills/five-slides-generator/`. Its `references/code-template.md` holds the
  pptxgenjs template and the design constants; `references/talking-points.md` holds the

  against the OneDrive originals.
- **One-pager** — the `html-to-pdf` skill, over HTML built with
  `~/DEV/TechEd_Prop/ShitfWave/baylor-brand.css`.

# House style

The department's own formats. Slide arc, timings, and standards below are transcribed
from `5_Sides_Content_Templates.docx` in
`~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-BaylorUniversity/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/07_EDUCATION/5slides5minutes/`
— that document is the primary source. Where this file and that document disagree, the
document wins and this file is wrong.

Four formats. **Two are wired to commands today** (deck, one-pager). Two are
transcribed and ready but not yet wired (social post, video script).

---

## The production order

From the source document, and worth keeping:

| Step | Action | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Build the 5-slide deck | Forces the core idea, the structure, and the takeaway. This is the foundation. |
| 2 | Write the social post | Distils the deck to its sharpest form. If it will not fit in 200 words, the deck needs work. |
| 3 | Script the video | The social post becomes the outline; adapt for spoken delivery. |

The one-pager slots in after step 1 for the same reason — it is the deck with the
talking points folded in, for a room you will not be standing in.

---

## Format 1 — the 5-slide deck  *(wired: `/deck`)*

### Standards

| Element | Standard |
|---|---|
| Duration | 5 minutes. Hard ceiling 7 minutes with Q&A. |
| Slides | **Exactly 5. No exceptions.** The constraint drives the clarity. |
| Audience | Cross-functional H&W staff — S&C, Athletic Medicine, Sport Science, Nutrition, Mental Health |
| Tone | Practitioner sharing with peers. Confident, accessible, not academic. |
| Depth | Surface-level *by design*. The goal is awareness plus one takeaway, not mastery. |
| Outcome | Spark curiosity. Ideally leads to a longer conversation or a full Performance School session. |

### The arc

| Slide | Time | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~45 sec | **THE HOOK** — title plus an opening question or scenario. Why should a room of diverse practitioners care? Make it cross-functional. |
| 2 | ~60 sec | **THE PROBLEM / CONTEXT** — the gap, misconception, or missed opportunity. A stat, a common scenario, or "what we typically see." Ground it in their daily reality. |
| 3 | ~75 sec | **THE INSIGHT** — the core concept. One big idea, clearly explained. A visual, analogy, or data point that sticks. No jargon that fails to cross disciplines. |
| 4 | ~60 sec | **THE APPLICATION** — so what? How it shows up across specialties. One or two examples, or "what this looks like on Monday." |
| 5 | ~45 sec | **THE TAKEAWAY** — one actionable thing. End with a question that invites the longer conversation. |

Backgrounds alternate **dark, light, dark, light, dark**. This is the visual signature
of the series; the `five-slides-generator` skill enforces it. Never break it.

### What to hand off

The `five-slides-generator` skill builds the `.pptx`. Give it, per slide: slide content
(the words on the slide) and talking points (what is said out loud). Plus:

```
TOPIC
CATEGORY            from topics/library.md
PRESENTER
CORE QUESTION       the one question this talk answers
THE ONE THING       the sentence they still know in a month
THE MISCONCEPTION   what they currently believe that is wrong
FOLLOW-UP POTENTIAL could this become a full Performance School session?
```

Its house rule, worth restating: *if you cannot explain the core idea in one sentence,
you are not ready to present it.* Scratch the surface on purpose — depth comes in the
follow-up conversation.

---

## Format 2 — the one-pager  *(wired: `/onepager`)*

**New format.** There is no template for it in the source document, so this is derived
from the deck arc and from the ShiftWave protocol card in
`~/DEV/TechEd_Prop/ShitfWave/` — the department's existing printed-artifact precedent.

### Standards

| Element | Standard |
|---|---|
| Size | One page, US Letter portrait. One page is the whole constraint. |
| Purpose | The deck for a room you are not standing in. Left on a desk, pinned in a training room, handed to a coach. |
| Audience | Same cross-functional staff, reading alone with no presenter |
| Tone | Same practitioner voice. Slightly more complete, because nobody is there to answer a question. |
| Brand | `~/DEV/TechEd_Prop/ShitfWave/baylor-brand.css` |
| Build | HTML, then the `html-to-pdf` skill. Never hand-laid-out. |

### The blocks

| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| Title + core question | The topic, and the one question this answers |
| The problem | Two to three sentences. The gap or misconception, grounded in their day. |
| The insight | The core concept, plus **one** visual. This is the block a reader remembers. |
| On Monday | Two or three concrete lines, split by specialty where that helps |
| The one thing | A single boxed sentence — the takeaway, quotable |
| Sources | Three to five, so the reader can check the work |
| Who to ask | Name and role, so a question has somewhere to go |

**Differences from the deck, deliberate:** sources are printed (a deck cites verbally),
and there is no discussion prompt (nobody is in the room), replaced by a contact line.

---

## Format 3 — the social post  *(transcribed, not yet wired)*

| Element | Standard |
|---|---|
| Platform | LinkedIn (long-form) or X (short-form) |
| Length | LinkedIn 150–250 words · X 280 characters, or a 3–5 post thread |
| Tone | Conversational, credible, practitioner-to-practitioner. Not academic, not salesy. |
| Structure | Hook → Insight → Takeaway → Engagement prompt |
| Visuals | Optional — one graphic, infographic, or quote card |
| Hashtags | 2–4 relevant tags |

| Section | Length | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Hook | 1–2 sentences | Stop the scroll. Question, surprising stat, or contrarian take. |
| Insight | 3–5 sentences | One concept explained clearly, with evidence or experience. |
| Takeaway | 1–2 sentences | One practical thing to do or think about differently. |
| Engage | 1 sentence | A question that invites practitioners to share their experience. |

Audience is **external** — peers and industry, not internal staff. Goal is thought
leadership and visibility.

---

## Format 4 — the video script  *(transcribed, not yet wired)*

| Element | Standard |
|---|---|
| Duration | 60–90 seconds. Hard ceiling 2 minutes. |
| Tone | Direct, conversational, confident. Talk to camera like a colleague, not a lecturer. |
| Format | Direct-to-camera, optional text overlays or simple graphics |
| Captions | Always. Most social video is watched with the sound off. |
| CTA | Every video ends with one clear takeaway or follow prompt. |

| Section | Time | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Hook | 5–10 sec | Bold statement or question. Land it in the first 3 seconds. |
| The Problem | 10–15 sec | The common mistake or misconception. Make the viewer feel seen. |
| The Insight | 20–30 sec | One concept, clearly explained. A stat or analogy if it helps. |
| The Fix | 15–20 sec | One practical action. "Try this tomorrow." |
| Close | 5–10 sec | Reinforce the point, then the prompt. |

House rule from the source: *write the way you talk. Read it out loud before filming.
If it sounds like a script, rewrite it until it sounds like you explaining something to
a colleague over coffee.*

---

## One topic, four formats

| | Social | Video | Deck | One-pager |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Audience** | External peers | External + internal | Internal H&W staff | Internal, reading alone |
| **Length** | 150–250 words | 60–90 sec | 5 min, 5 slides | 1 page |
| **Depth** | One insight + one takeaway | Problem → insight → fix | Hook → problem → insight → application → takeaway | Deck, plus sources |
| **Goal** | Thought leadership | Awareness, shareability | Spark curiosity | Reference after the room empties |

The core idea never changes across formats. Depth, length, and audience do. All four are
written from the **same brief** — see `briefs/README.md`.

---

## Where the rendering lives

Do not reproduce any of this in code here.

- **Deck** — the `five-slides-generator` skill at
  `~/.claude/skills/five-slides-generator/`. Its `references/code-template.md` holds the
  pptxgenjs template and the design constants; `references/talking-points.md` holds the
  per-slide timing budget (~4:45 total). Its copies are current — verified 2026-08-18
  against the OneDrive originals.
- **One-pager** — the `html-to-pdf` skill, over HTML built with
  `~/DEV/TechEd_Prop/ShitfWave/baylor-brand.css`.

=== PRINT-SPECS === # Print & lamination spec — Shiftwave Protocol Card Hand this page to the print shop along with the press PDF. **Send them:** `Shiftwave-Protocol-Card-C-Matrix-PRESS-bleed.pdf` **Not** the plain `…C-Matrix.pdf` — that one is trimmed to 8.5×11 with no bleed and is the desk-reference / email copy. ## Page | | | |---|---| | Final trim size | **8.5 × 11 in**, portrait | | Supplied artwork | **8.75 × 11.25 in** (verified: MediaBox 630 × 810 pt) | | Bleed | **0.125 in (3.175 mm)** all four sides | | Safe margin | All critical content sits ≥ 0.39 in inside trim | | Pages | 1, single-sided | | Fonts | Embedded and subset in the PDF — no font files needed | ## Lamination - **5 mil matte, both sides.** Matte is not optional here. The card is a dark ground at **~83% ink coverage**; under gloss it will mirror the ceiling lights in the facility and become unreadable at exactly the angle an athlete reads it from. - **Sealed edge**, 1/8 in laminate border beyond trim. - **Rounded corners, 1/4 in (6 mm) radius** — square corners on a 5 mil laminate lift and catch, and these get handled with taped or wet hands. ### If it needs to hang Do **not** punch a hole in the card itself. The masthead starts 0.24 in from the top trim, so a standard 0.375 in punch lands in the Baylor lockup. Either: - ask for a **0.5 in laminate tab** above the trim line and punch through laminate only, or - mount with industrial velcro / 3M command strip on the back. ## Ink and colour - The ground is **`#1E1F1F`** with a Baylor green wash. Ask for a **rich black build**, not 100% K. A single-channel black at this coverage prints mottled and grey-brown, and the green wash disappears. - Brand colours as supplied: **Baylor Green `#154734`**, **Baylor Gold `#FFB81C`**.
